proposed_fixes.title: Preserve held Shift when emitting a remapped numpad navigation key
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Shift changes the virtual-key identity produced by numpad navigation keys, and remap normalization can consume the Shift transition or emit the arrow without carrying the held modifier to the target application.
plan: Create an engine test for NumPad6→Right with Shift held before and after NumPad6 key-down.
Normalize numpad-origin identity for lookup without clearing unrelated held modifiers.
Ensure injected Right uses the correct extended-key flag while physical Shift remains visible to the target until release.
verification: Verify Shift+NumPad6 selects text exactly like Shift+Right.
Verify Ctrl+NumPad6 continues to move by word.
Run numpad-origin, NumLock on/off, left/right Shift, and key-up ordering tests.

confidence.rationale: The report and duplicate are specific and current code shows this special-case area, but later numpad fixes may already cover part of the scenario.

issue_context.summary: When a numpad key is remapped to an arrow key, holding physical Shift does not extend text selection as Shift+physical-arrow does; Ctrl combinations continue to work.
known_information: PowerToys 0.63; NumPad6 is remapped to Right.
Both left and right Shift are ignored with the remapped key, while Ctrl works.
The editor itself has difficulty recording Shift+numpad combinations.
inferences: Shift-driven numpad virtual-key translation is colliding with remap lookup or modifier preservation.
issue_context.analysis: The current engine now tracks numpad origin explicitly, making a focused regression test cheap and decisive; no reporter diagnostics are needed first.

reproduce.title: Test numpad modifier preservation
prerequisites: Enable Num Lock as appropriate for NumPad6
Open a text editor with a line of text
steps: Hold left Shift and press NumPad6; repeat with right Shift.
Repeat with physical Right as a control.
Repeat with Ctrl+NumPad6 and with Num Lock toggled.
reproduce.expected_result: Shift+NumPad6 selects text like Shift+Right, Ctrl behavior remains correct, and no modifier sticks.
